summary: Kinney Point on the Payette National Forest: camp in the 1920s, L-4 cab built 1932, burned 1951; now a Forest Service interpretive site with a sign.

facts.status_note: Burned in 1951; the site is a Forest Service interpretive stop; no source describes what, if anything, of the lookout remains

access.note: Forest Service interpretive site with a large wooden sign

visit.trail_note: Rocky, rough spur road; Forest Service says passenger cars are not recommended; no restrooms or potable water

events.note: Burned per Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says gone 1951; Idaho Fire Lookouts says destroyed 1951
July 1953 Hells Canyon celebration at Kinney Point; more than 1,000 expected

evidence.supports: Camp in the 1920s, L-4 cab 1932, gone 1951
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists 1951 as destroyed
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists 1932 L-4 cab
More than 1,000 expected at Kinney Point
evidence.quote: More than 1,000 spectators are expected to attend the fete at Kinney Point

evidence.supports: Regional head of the Forest Service to speak at the Hells Canyon celebration
evidence.quote: regional head of the Forest Service, Ogden, will be the principal speaker

evidence.supports: Forest Service site overlooks Hells Canyon; once home to a fire lookout; large wooden sign
evidence.quote: Overlooking Hells Canyon, this peak was once home to a fire lookout. A large wooden sign shares information about this site.

evidence.supports: Spur road rocky and rough; passenger cars not recommended
evidence.quote: The spur road to Kinney Point is rocky and rough; passenger cars are not recommended.
Restrooms are not available at this site.

evidence.quote: Potable water is not available at this site.

notes_for_editor: No staffing history: Idaho Fire Lookouts says none is documented, so staffing is left out of the story. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1945 National Geodetic Survey station description that mentions a lookout house corner; its record is marked Removed and does not describe what survives, so it is not used. The Forest Service page is the public listing for the site; the spur road is rough.
